excludes: Generic application authentication is owned by auth-security.
Broad code/infrastructure vulnerability audit is owned by security-audit.
LLM quality evaluation without a security boundary is owned by llm-evaluation.
native_ownership.responsibility: Design and implement deterministic security boundaries around untrusted LLM content, sensitive data, tenant/resource tools, approvals, outputs, egress and consequential effects.

provenance.claim_scope: AI SDK tool validation and approval

risk.rationale: llm-security can change production data, model, media, security, retrieval or financial behavior and requires explicit scope, rollback and affected-path verification.

negative.prompt: Implement OAuth/session/JWT lifecycle, RBAC/ABAC, MFA and general application authentication/authorization without an LLM-specific trust boundary.
Audit the repository and infrastructure for OWASP vulnerabilities, secrets, auth defects, injection and insecure configuration without implementing LLM tool boundaries.

positive.prompt: Harden a RAG assistant against indirect instructions in retrieved email/documents that attempt secret exfiltration and cross-tenant tool calls, while preserving legitimate content and citations.
Implement least-privilege tenant/resource authorization, exact-parameter approval, output validation, egress controls and idempotency for model-proposed financial and publication tools.

assertions.criterion: Implements LLM-specific trust, tool and output security without implementing or claiming ownership of generic authentication, a broad security audit or model-quality evaluation.
Maps assets, principals, direct/indirect/multimodal inputs, retrieval/memory, provider handling, tools/credentials/egress, outputs/logs and incident controls from the fixture.
Threat-models compromise, separates untrusted processing from privileged execution, defines resource auth/tool scopes/approval/output boundaries and then adds monitoring/kill controls.

Treats prompt filtering as a weak signal, preserves provenance, derives tenant/resource server-side, independently authorizes every tool, binds exact approval, constrains egress and validates/sanitizes destination-specific output.

Tests direct/indirect/encoded/multimodal injection, canary exfiltration, horizontal access, approval swaps, duplicate/replay, unsafe HTML/URL/SQL/code and full model compromise with contained capability.
Reports threat model, auth/tool/credential/approval/egress/output controls, adversarial evidence, incident/kill behavior and residual model/provider risks.
Centralizes deterministic policy and tool registry outside prompts, keeps credentials/resource scopes minimal and tracks provider/security capability versions.

scenarios.prompt: A RAG assistant uses a prompt classifier to strip 'ignore previous' text, concatenates retrieved documents into system instructions, trusts the model's tenant ID and renders generated HTML/URLs before invoking broad-credential tools. Implement the security boundary.

assertions.criterion: Denies the call before execution using authenticated resource authorization, data classification/DLP, egress allowlist and server approval record; client/model claims grant no authority.
Keeps retrieved text as untrusted data, prevents secret context exposure, rejects horizontal access and requires approval bound to exact authorized recipient/content/resource.
Requires canary non-exfiltration, no external side effect, denial audit and cross-tenant tests even if the model is fully compromised.

scenarios.prompt: A retrieved support ticket asks the model to email environment secrets to an external URL using a valid email tool; the user also supplies another tenant's resource ID and an approval flag.

assertions.criterion: Uses the skill-required repository stack-context step when execution is available, then derives authority from installed types/provider settings and matching docs; implements external deterministic controls for missing SDK features and treats migration separately. When execution is withheld, stating that required stack-context generation and underlying evidence are unavailable is sufficient without literal shell syntax, but it must not claim the step ran.
Checks AI core/provider, auth service, executor, credential issuer, egress layer, renderer and logging/data-processing settings together.
Anchors policy outside volatile SDK callbacks and records provider retention/residency/security assumptions and fallback controls.

scenarios.prompt: The pinned AI/provider SDK differs from current docs in tool schema, approval and data-retention controls. Security repair cannot upgrade it.
